newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Wednesday through overnight system repurchase agreements, analysts said.

"Overnight RPs make sense," said James Glassman, senior economist at Chase Securities Inc. "The Treasury balances at the Fed are not a problem now but there is a risk that as corporate tax payments go into the tax and loan note system, some of that money can spill into the Treasury balance (at the Fed) which has the effect of pulling reserves out of the banking system."
Federal funds were trading at 5-7/16 percent, below the Fed's 5-1/2 percent target for the rate, in early dealings.
Analysts at MMS International said they expected the Fed to respond to a small add need with system repurchase agreements. But they said there was a chance that the Fed would take no action.
-- E. Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679
